A1.justification: Both complete PDFs describe the same universality framework and four theoretical applications. Their text, equations, figures and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v3 presents mathematical theorems, analytical network examples and proofs. Neither the main text nor the appendix reports original empirical results.

after.justification: v4 remains entirely theoretical. Its four applications and expanded proof appendix contain no experimental, simulation or data-analysis outcomes.

M1.justification: Section 5 replaces unrestricted real output-weight matrices C_i with products of unit spheres, restricting their columns to unit vectors. The feature-map formula, network composition and ridgelet construction otherwise remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or evaluates tasks or test scenarios. The four network examples are theoretical applications, not empirical coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates comparison methods against the proposed construction. Named architectures and previous methods are discussed theoretically.

E3.justification: Both versions lack experimental protocols, training budgets, evaluation metrics and testing procedures. The revised mathematical parameter domain is not an experimental setting change.

E4.justification: Neither version reports ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity studies or empirical case analyses. The additional geometric discussion is interpretation rather than an added analysis.

E5.justification: Repeated runs, seeds, uncertainty estimates and statistical tests are absent from both versions.

E6.justification: Neither version reports measured performance, rankings or observed empirical findings. Changes to mathematical statements are covered under T1.

T1.justification: Corollary 1 corrects the parameter-distribution domain, changes the ridgelet integration domain from Ξ to X and fixes layer-parameter indexing. Section 5 restricts the parameter domain, and v3's Haar-measure subsection is removed. Remark 2(2) now states reconstruction without the earlier scalar factor. The main reconstruction theorems remain; Appendix A.3–A.8 chiefly reorganizes existing derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract's unified constructive universality claim and four applications are retained. However, v4 removes the introduction's separate contribution claim concerning the construction of irreducible representations for the examples.

C2.justification: Section 3.1.1 adds an alternative bundle/section interpretation, while Sections 2.2 and 8 emphasize universality through irreducibility and simple objects. Remark 2 adds a projection interpretation for redundant parameterizations and revises the regularity caveat. The new 'zero or identity' explanation in Section 2.2 conflicts with Theorem 2's scalar-multiple statement.

D1.justification: Neither version provides implementation settings, hardware, training times or code/data access instructions. The expanded appendix concerns mathematical derivations rather than experimental reproducibility.

R1.justification: v4 adds Cohen, Geiger and Weiler (2019), A General Theory of Equivariant CNNs on Homogeneous Spaces, to position the section interpretation. The introduction also replaces the explicit joint-invariance bottleneck discussion of Sonoda et al. (2024a) with a broader attribution of inspiration.

P1.justification: v4 substantially rewrites the introduction, geometric interpretation and discussion; separates the machine and ridgelet-transform subsections; removes the calculus subsection; and moves several inline proofs into dedicated appendix subsections. Notation and Ikeda's affiliation/contact information are also revised.

P2.justification: v4 removes the fiber-bundle diagram previously numbered Figure 2 and enlarges the two retained schematics. Former Figure 3 becomes Figure 2 beside Section 4. Equation numbering is removed and displays are reformatted, while the single-column layout remains.

improvement.justification: v4 repairs Corollary 1's domain and indexing errors and makes the retained proof dependencies easier to follow. However, its new Section 2.2 explanation incorrectly limits Schur's scalar multiples to 'zero or identity', and Remark 2(2) drops the reconstruction scalar without explaining normalization. The balance between clearer organization, formula corrections and new mathematical imprecision does not support a reliable net-quality judgment.
